summary: The study focuses on area-selective atomic layer deposition (ALD) of titanium nitride (TiN) using a passivation layer formed by trimethoxy(octadecyl)silane (TMODS). The research evaluates the effectiveness of different siloxane precursors for passivation, with TMODS showing the best performance. The ALD process is conducted at 350 °C, and the study demonstrates high selectivity (>0.99) for TiN deposition up to 20 nm thickness. The passivation layer inhibits ALD on non-growth areas, enabling precise deposition on patterned surfaces.
evidence: The study demonstrates the use of trimethoxy(octadecyl)silane (TMODS) as a passivation layer for area-selective ALD of TiN. The ALD process is conducted at 350 °C, and the selectivity is reported to be higher than 0.99 up to 20 nm film thickness. The passivation layer suppresses precursor adsorption, allowing for precise deposition on patterned surfaces.
